locator.quote:  The internal compressor overheated and turned off. You may have exceeded the duty cycle for the system. See Understand duty-cycle limitations on page 50. | 1. Allow the power supply to cool for 4 minutes. Leave the system on to allow the fan to cool the power supply. Then try to produce an arc by pulling the torch trigger. When the internal compressor overheats, the compressor turns off, and the compressor and temperature LEDs remain illuminated for 4 minutes. The system does not prevent you from firing the torch before the 4 minutes elapses. However, if you begin cutting before the compressor has time to fully cool down, the same fault is likely to occur again. If the fault LEDs persist, continue with the following troubleshooting steps in the order listed.

5 – Troubleshooting and System Tests
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_92286646262199641a60d2de0e6a]]
Temperature LED faults
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_b3372f497ab6f464b9276c34255c]]
The temperature LED illuminates while the machine is powered ON.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_920515fa159ff09ec813d7c74411]]
Possible causes
Possible solutions
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_eeac7ebed01ffc41cc17f9df20d7]]

The system overheated because the duty 
cycle was exceeded.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_34d2929cb2021bf13ec84f3ef562]]

The system is too cold to operate. The 
ambient temperature is too low.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_aa4880250408dabf330cf02df166]]

Let the system cool before using it. Leave 
the system on to allow the fan to cool the 
power supply. The fan runs for 7 minutes 
after postflow. See Understand duty-cycle 
limitations on page 50.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_f74a2ec3266183489e8e5561a57b]]

Perform Test 8 – fan on page 95.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_a0a020ab5f313eaf1c4d4e88c58d]]

Let the system warm up before using it. The 
operating temperature range for this system 
is -10°C (14°F) to 40°C (104°F).
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_e22bd2b3dddc066e9c6b693b13c1]]
The temperature LED blinks while the machine is powered ON.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_a8bcd12f763fae366ae18a8a26d6]]
Possible causes
Possible solutions
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_e1d9f1b76c5fb60346962154dfe2]]
This fault occurs when the system continuously 
draws too much input current for too long. The fault 
protects the power switch and power cord from 
damage caused by overheating. This fault most often 
occurs when:
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_a422c658fc549ed15529c4690d58]]

You are operating the system on a 120 VAC 
input circuit and the cutting current is set 
above 20 A.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_b826be28fa77a303ba06bb7cac9b]]

You are operating the system on a 
120 V / 15 A circuit.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_37d4007f638aaa41def199d9bb8b]]

You are operating the system on a 120 VAC 
input circuit and are frequently stretching the 
arc while cutting.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_649394f9f9c6ddc0e2f53919c097]]

You are using an extension cord that is too 
long.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_ae59bb7842a1f6346d621a87b15c]]
The maximum length for an extension 
cord on a 120 VAC input circuit is 16 m 
(53 feet). The maximum length for an 
extension cord on a 240 VAC input 
circuit is 40.5 m (133 feet).
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_370b48e8975a5f9198b5085d6fbc]]
Let the system cool for 3 minutes before using it. 
Leave the system on to allow the fan to cool the 
power supply.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_8e0f72cc76dfc6de7c4b8da2ccba]]
To prevent the fault from occurring:
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_f50caf249398623a84af85d98dbd]]

Operate the system on a 240 VAC input 
circuit whenever possible.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_d88af82c7594383dcfd0881765d2]]

Turn down the cutting current. See 
Step 3 – Adjust the output current on 
page 47.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_829f1d51592beac5942d9e32d129]]

If you do operate the system on a120 VAC 
input circuit, use a 20 A circuit and set the 
cutting current below 20 A.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_7ac6321269707cbd32bd6090d620]]

Avoid stretching the arc. Drag the torch on 
the workpiece. See Edge start on a 
workpiece on page 54.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_c3d0cabb5904845cd3a4a22019cf]]

Operate the system without using an 
extension cord. If you must use an extension 
cord, use a heavy conductor cord of the 
shortest possible length. See Extension 
cord recommendations on page 33.
[[EVIDENCE_ID: ev_d38ce8b6d7d2c63d46ba6c622f33]]
